image_prompt: Mr. Darling is a distinguished middle-aged gentleman with a dignified bearing befitting upper-class Edwardian society. He has a lean, methodical build suggesting careful restraint and practical sensibility. His face is angular and contemplative, with sharp, intelligent eyes that betray both pride and quiet worry. He possesses a neat, well-trimmed beard tinged with grey, and his hair is slicked back with Victorian precision. His expression carries an underlying tension between social propriety and suppressed emotion—the faint creases around his eyes suggest a man perpetually calculating expenses and neighbors' opinions. He wears impeccably tailored evening dress: a formal black coat with pristine white shirt and silk cravat, polished waistcoat suggesting financial conscientiousness. His posture is erect yet slightly strained, as though bearing invisible burdens of responsibility and social standing. Every detail speaks of a man devoted to honor and propriety, yet touched by an ineffable melancholy—a tender vulnerability beneath his pedantic exterior. His hands are refined, capable, suggesting both gentleness and the grip of someone who has worked to secure his family's position. There is gentle irony in his formal perfection, a hint of wistfulness in his gaze.
